elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New 9.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience..." — covers both the Agreement and any Order Form, and is an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a true convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: New 9.4 requires "thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or approval requirements attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: New 9.4: "Vendor shall refund, on a pro-rata basis, all prepaid Fees covering the period after the effective date of termination." Pro rata is express (not merely inferred from post-termination coverage) and reaches all prepaid Fees as defined in 1.5, not just the narrower "prepaid recurring Fees" in retained 10.2.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: New 9.4 second sentence: "Vendor may not terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term." Retained 9.1–9.3 give Vendor only for-cause and insolvency rights, so no residual Vendor convenience right survives.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 9.4 sets 30 days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band. This is more favourable to Customer but does not literally satisfy the fallback element; the preferred level is the operative target.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither the retained termination provisions (9.1–9.5) nor the new 9.4 imposes any early-termination fee, penalty, or contingent payment on Customer, so there is no fee to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori — 9.4 bars Vendor convenience termination entirely during a committed term, and no other clause grants Vendor a no-cause exit, so Vendor cannot exit mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor has no convenience termination right at all under the amended Section 9, so no notice period is required.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted 9.4 carries all four preferred elements in operative language (convenience right over Agreement or any Order Form; 30 days' written notice; express pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees for the post-termination period; express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term).

Finding status 'missing' is correct: retained 9.1–9.3 are for-cause, insolvency and incident-based only, and 8.1 fixes a three-year term, so the absence of any Customer no-cause exit in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation by missing behaviour.

Minimal: one concise insertion into the existing Section 9 numbering, with no deletions or paraphrase elsewhere. The model-language surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted, and no extras (survival tails, expense allocation, procedures) were added.

Intent preserved: retained 10.2 (refund of prepaid recurring Fees plus breach-related refunds) and 9.5 (cumulative remedies, Order Form severability) survive without contradiction — 9.5 expressly makes termination rights additive, so the broader 9.4 refund and the narrower 10.2 refund coexist. No dangling cross-references or undefined terms are created; "Fees" and "Order Form" are defined in 1.5 and 1.6, and "committed term" is grounded in the fixed three-year term in 8.1 and Order Form terms.
Fallback level is not independently satisfied only because notice is 30 days rather than 60–90; no repair is needed since the preferred level is complete.
